quick: Oral PUVA: 10-70 mg by weight, 1.5-2 h before UVA; UVADEX: treatment volume x 0.017 mL extracorporeal
Oral: take with low-fat food or milk to reduce GI upset
May cause fetal harm; avoid, advise against pregnancy
Excretion in milk unknown; use caution
Avoid hepatotoxic agents; alcohol may add risk
Eye exams, skin/photosensitivity, CBC and LFTs, BP during photopheresis
summary: Methoxsalen is a psoralen that, after photoactivation by long-wave UVA light, forms DNA adducts inhibiting DNA synthesis and cell proliferation. Oral methoxsalen plus UVA (PUVA) treats severe recalcitrant psoriasis and vitiligo; the UVADEX sterile solution is used extracorporeally with the THERAKOS photopheresis system for palliation of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Strict photoprotection of skin and eyes is mandatory.
indications: Symptomatic control of severe, recalcitrant, disabling psoriasis unresponsive to other therapy (oral PUVA, biopsy-confirmed)
Repigmentation of idiopathic vitiligo (oral methoxsalen with UVA)
Palliative treatment of skin manifestations of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma unresponsive to other treatment (UVADEX extracorporeal photopheresis)

dosage.n: Take with low-fat food/milk; not more than every other day

dosage.d: 20 mg daily, 2-4 h before measured UVA or sunlight exposure
Treatment volume x 0.017 = mL UVADEX injected into recirculation bag
dosage.n: Do not inject directly into patient; single-use vial (20 mcg/mL)

admin: Oral capsules taken 1.5-2 hours before UVA exposure with low-fat food or milk
Establish minimum phototoxic dose and peak phototoxic time before photochemotherapy
UVADEX is for extracorporeal use only via the THERAKOS CELLEX system - never inject directly into patient
Do not dilute UVADEX; discard any drawn into a plastic syringe for more than 1 hour
Wear UVA-absorbing wrap-around sunglasses and protect skin for 24 hours after each treatment
moa: The exact mechanism is unknown. Methoxsalen, upon photoactivation by UVA, forms covalent monofunctional and bifunctional (cross-link) adducts with DNA, inhibiting DNA synthesis, cell division and epidermal turnover. In photopheresis, the photoactivated leukocyte mixture is reinfused and may trigger an immune-mediated response against malignant T-cells.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to methoxsalen or other psoralens
Light-sensitive diseases (lupus erythematosus, porphyrias, xeroderma pigmentosum, albinism)
Melanoma or history of melanoma; invasive squamous cell carcinoma
relative: Prior skin cancer or arsenic/ionizing radiation exposure

preg: Methoxsalen may cause fetal harm; animal studies showed fetal mortality, resorptions and skeletal malformations. There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Women of childbearing potential should avoid pregnancy; apprise of fetal hazard if used.
lact: It is not known whether methoxsalen is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in milk, exercise caution when administered to a nursing woman.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is established in the labeling.
hepatic: Methoxsalen is metabolized by the liver; use with caution in hepatic impairment and avoid additional hepatotoxic agents.

major: Concomitant photosensitizing agents (anthralin, coal tar, griseofulvin, phenothiazines, nalidixic acid, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, thiazides, halogenated salicylanilides) - markedly increased photosensitivity/burn risk
moderate: Staining dyes (methylene blue, toluidine blue, rose bengal, methyl orange) - photosensitivity
Prior or concurrent ionizing radiation, arsenic, tar/UVB - increased skin cancer risk
minor: Foods high in furocoumarins (limes, figs, parsley, celery, mustard) may add to photosensitivity
interactions.food: Take oral doses with low-fat food or milk to reduce nausea; bioavailability and onset vary by formulation.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxins during therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC, LFTs and antinuclear antibody where indicated during long-term PUVA.

common: Hypotension (photopheresis, related to extracorporeal volume shifts)
serious: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma with PUVA (incidence ~17.6x expected)
rare: Arrhythmia during photopheresis in patients with cardiac disease

monitoring: Ophthalmologic examination at baseline and periodically (cataract/retinal risk)
Skin examination for actinic damage and skin cancers during and after PUVA
CBC, liver and renal function periodically with long-term therapy
Blood pressure and cardiovascular status during photopheresis sessions
counsel: Wear UVA-blocking wrap-around sunglasses for 24 hours after each dose, indoors and out
Cover skin or use SPF 15+ sunblock and avoid additional sun/UV exposure after treatment
Take oral capsules at the exact interval before UVA prescribed, with low-fat food or milk
Report eye problems, severe skin reactions or new skin lesions promptly
Avoid other photosensitizing drugs and furocoumarin-rich foods
Use effective contraception and avoid pregnancy during therapy
pk: Photosensitization onset ~1-2 h after oral capsule
Store at 15-30 C (59-86 F); UVADEX in amber glass vials
pearls: PUVA (oral methoxsalen + UVA) is carcinogenic - cumulative squamous cell carcinoma risk is dose-related
UVADEX dose for each photopheresis treatment = treatment volume x 0.017 mL; never inject into patient
Strict 24-hour eye and skin photoprotection after every dose is essential
Aphakia is an absolute contraindication due to retinal damage risk
Concomitant photosensitizing drugs sharply raise burn risk
missed: For oral PUVA, doses are tied to scheduled UVA treatments - do not take an extra dose to make up a missed one; reschedule the supervised treatment with the prescriber. Never take methoxsalen without the planned, controlled UVA exposure.
overdose: In the event of overdose, keep the patient in a darkened room for at least 24 hours and provide supportive care. Avoid all UV/sunlight exposure until photosensitivity resolves.
